newsitem.title: NORWAY: Elkem mulls output cuts due to high power costs.
newsitem.headline: Elkem mulls output cuts due to high power costs.

text.p: Norwegian metals producer Elkem ASA is considering cutting production at some plants due to record high domestic power prices this year, a spokesman for the company said on Thursday.

"We are continually going through our portfolio to examine where it is not cost-efficient to produce," said Elkem spokesman Ola Boesterud. "Where it is not cost-efficient, we will take out some furnaces."
Boesterud said it was too early to identify areas where production may be cut.
Earlier this year Elkem shut a ferrosilicon furnace at Bjoelvefossen.
Elkem is Norway's second largest electricity consumer after industrial giant Norsk Hydro ASA, using around 9,000 gigawatt hours (GWh) per year.
The company produces about 3,000 GWh per year, secures 5,000 GWh under long-term contracts and buys the remaining 1,000 GWh under near-term contracts.
Norway relies on hydro-based power for electricity production. Power prices have surged to record levels this year after low snow and rainfall last winter.
The oil and gas-rich country has been forced to increase power imports from Denmark and Sweden to avoid a shortfall of supplies next winter.

In August, Elkem said a shortfall in captive power production and higher than average spot electricity prices had added 20 million crowns to the group's power costs during the first six dmonths of the year.
